Subject: Spike in June invoice — possible duplicate charges?

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

We received the June invoice this morning and there is an unexpected spike compared to last month (line items show ~3.2M tokens billed vs ~1.1M typical). Attached is the invoice PDF and a quick screenshot from our billing system. Can you confirm whether this is a real usage change or a billing error on Redwood's side? Our finance team needs a resolution before we finalize the payment run on Friday.

Key bits:
- Customer account: Acme Corp (ACME-789)
- Invoice total: $14,632.47 (June 2026)
- Expected ~ $5k range historically

Please let us know next steps and what data you need from our side.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in June invoice — possible duplicate charges? — preliminary findings

Jordan — quick update from billing and ops after a first pass: we pulled a token-level export for ACME-789 and compared the ingestion events to the billing pipeline. Two things stood out: 

1) There was a short-lived spike in ingestion around 2026-06-15 02:00-03:00 UTC driven by a client-side retry storm after a regional load-balancer misconfiguration. Approximately 1.9M extra tokens were recorded during that window.

2) During the same window, an internal telemetry router bug prevented request-id propagation for ~18% of requests routed through the proxy. That omission caused our deduplication step to miss a subset of duplicate requests, effectively double-counting tokens for those flows.

We’ve attached a CSV (acme_june_usage_breakdown.csv) with the per-hour token counts and the subset of sessions that were affected. Based on the audit, the over-billed delta is ~1.85M tokens (~$3,214).

Proposed immediate fix:
- Issue a credit note for $3,214 against June invoice (we’ll generate a formal credit PDF).
- Share a short postmortem describing root cause and the technical mitigations.
- Implement a fix in the telemetry router to propagate request-id consistently + add a near-term post-ingest dedupe check.

We’ll follow up with dates for the permanent remediation and when the credit will appear on your account. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your forecasting.

Marissa Cole
Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_june_usage_breakdown.csv (csv)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>

Thanks Marissa — that explanation is helpful and the CSV matches what we see on our side. Two quick asks from Acme finance/procurement: 

1) We need a formal credit note and an updated invoice line item before our payment run on Friday (2026-06-25).
2) Can you include a short timeline in the postmortem (what happened, when it was fixed, and how you’ll prevent it from recurring)? Our auditors will want to see the steps.

If you can send the credit note and the postmortem link by EOD Monday (2026-06-22) that would close the loop for us.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Jordan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Charge variance — postmortem and credit plan

Jordan — attaching the formal postmortem and the credit note. Summary below: 

Root cause: Short-lived client retry storm + telemetry router dropped request-id header on a subset of proxied requests, preventing our dedupe step from identifying duplicates.

What we fixed (timeline):
- 2026-06-15 03:20 UTC — load-balanced routing rule corrected to stop retry storm (mitigation).
- 2026-06-16 01:10 UTC — telemetry router patch deployed to enforce request-id propagation (hotfix).
- 2026-06-20 04:00 UTC — post-ingest dedupe check added to billing pipeline for the affected time windows (safety net).

Customer impact: ~1.85M tokens double-counted; estimated over-bill $3,214.00.
Action items completed:
- Credit note generated: credit_note_ACME-789.pdf — you should see the adjusted invoice in your portal within 48 hours and the credit applied to the June invoice.
- Postmortem published: https://drive.google.com/redwood/postmortems/ACME-June-2026 (public link to the document for your accounting/audit team).
- We’ve scheduled a follow-up change to add request-id enforcement at the edge proxy (ETA 2026-07-05) and a monthly audit to detect similar anomalies.

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_june2026.pdf, credit_note_ACME-789.pdf

If you need the documents emailed to a different address for your AP team, tell us where to send them and we’ll route immediately.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
SRE — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
